faq.question: How much does window replacement cost in Menlo Park?
faq.answer: Menlo Park homeowners typically invest $10,000 to $25,000 for a full window replacement project. This prestigious Peninsula community — home to Sand Hill Road venture capital and Stanford-adjacent neighborhoods — features large single-family homes where premium window specifications are routine. Projects covering 15–25 windows with Andersen or Marvin are common. Single window installation starts at approximately $750.

faq.question: Do I need a permit to replace windows in Menlo Park?
faq.answer: Yes. Menlo Park requires a building permit for window replacements. Our team handles all permit applications with the City of Menlo Park's Community Development Department on your behalf.

faq.question: Is it worth replacing 20-year-old windows in Menlo Park?
faq.answer: Often yes. Twenty-year-old windows in Menlo Park commonly show fogged glass, drafts and weak locks. Newer ENERGY STAR units improve comfort and curb appeal; Deluxe Windows compares payback against your utility rates and home style before recommending replacement.

faq.question: Should I choose fiberglass or vinyl windows in Menlo Park?
faq.answer: Vinyl is the value pick for most Menlo Park replacements and handles Bay Area weather well. Fiberglass (including Marvin Ultrex) is stronger, more stable in temperature swings and better for larger openings or coastal exposure. We show both side by side in the showroom and on-site.

faq.question: How long does window replacement take in Menlo Park?
faq.answer: Most Menlo Park projects are measured in one visit and installed in one to three working days once products arrive — typically four to eight weeks after ordering, depending on brand and custom sizes.
